title: Carbon–carbon bond formation and organic synthesis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR26a#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR26a#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR26a#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR26a#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR26a#N.4, OR26a#N.8a, OR26a#N.11, OR26a#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Propanenitrile
items.clue: CH₃CH₂CN, made by refluxing bromoethane with KCN in ethanol.

items.label: Hydroxynitrile
items.clue: Formed when CN⁻ adds across the C=O of an aldehyde or ketone, e.g. CH₃CH(OH)CN.

items.label: Cyanide
items.clue: ⁻:C≡N, the simplest carbon donor of a lone pair; it lengthens a chain by one carbon.

items.label: Nucleophilic substitution
items.clue: Mechanism in which the lone pair on CN⁻ attacks a δ+ carbon and the C–Br electrons go to Br.

questions.stem: 1-Bromobutane is heated under reflux with potassium cyanide in ethanol. What is the organic product?
questions.explanation: CN⁻ replaces Br: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CN. Five carbons, including the C≡N carbon.

questions.stem: 2-Hydroxypropanenitrile, CH₃CH(OH)CN, is heated under reflux with dilute hydrochloric acid. What is the organic product?
questions.explanation: C≡N → –COOH, with NH₄Cl as the by-product. CH₃CH(OH)COOH is lactic acid.

questions.stem: Which pair of reactants, in dry ether followed by dilute acid, gives butan-2-ol, CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃?
questions.explanation: The ethyl group bonds to the C=O carbon of ethanal: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃, a secondary alcohol.

questions.stem: Bromomethane, CH₃Br, has one carbon. Which route turns it into ethylamine, CH₃CH₂NH₂?

options.text: Heat with excess ammonia in ethanol in a sealed tube
Reflux with KCN in ethanol, then hydrolyse with dilute acid
Reflux with KCN in ethanol, then reduce the nitrile
Warm with aqueous NaOH, then heat the product with ammonia

questions.explanation: CN⁻ adds one carbon: CH₃CN, ethanenitrile. Reduction turns –C≡N into –CH₂NH₂: CH₃CH₂NH₂.
